item.title: Dry eyes are common among women. Here's why you shouldn't ignore it
item.description: Dry eyes are a very common chronic eye condition among women in perimenopause and beyond. Here's why you shouldn't ignore it.

item.title: They live by a shrine to a saint. Why are their homes being demolished?
item.description: The neighborhood is a pilgrimage site, with a shrine to the Sufi saint known as Bari Imam. In the past year, hundreds of homes of the working poor were razed. Residents fear more will be demolished.

item.title: Whatever happened to the U.S. famine alert system that Trump shut down, then reopened

item.title: NPR's 2-year search for the truth about deaths from heat
item.description: An investigation from NPR and Boston University finds that heat kills thousands of Americans every year. But official numbers radically undercount heat deaths.

item.title: Why too many women are prescribed antibiotics for UTIs they don't have
item.description: A recent study found that many women treated for recurrent UTIs didn't have UTIs at all. Instead, their symptoms were caused by hormonally driven inflammation and pelvic floor dysfunction.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Medicare's pilot GLP-1 discount program has a catch. Some sick patients don't qualify
item.description: Medicare launched a pilot program that could streamline the process to get GLP-1s, with some seniors paying just $50 a month. But many people with the most serious illnesses won't get that discount.

item.title: The bridges of Rwanda open up new worlds
item.description: A charity built 96 bridges to connect communities separated by rivers and gorges. A new study looks at the life-changing impact of a concrete-and-steel pedestrian crossing.
